catalog_quote: Rix 1998, 60, assumed a separation of Raetic and Etruscan a few centuries prior to their attestation; he dated Proto-Tyrsenian to around the turn from the second to the first millennium BC. Schumacher 2004, 316f., further points to the lack of any Raetic evidence for syncope triggered by protosyllabic stress, which is so characteristic for Etruscan from the 5th century onwards. In Etruscan, sporadic variation between vowels in non-initial syllables already in the 7th century shows that the dynamic protosyllabic accent dates at least to archaic Etruscan (Rix 1985, 217); Schumacher concludes that this accent pattern in Etruscan is prehistoric, and that Raetic, which either had no protosyllabic stress or none strong enough to lead to syncopation, was already distant from Etruscan at that time, but cf. Rix 1985, 117f., and Agostiniani 1992, 52.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No positive statement of stress placement exists. The only claim is negative and inferential: unlike Etruscan (which had a strong word-initial, 'protosyllabic' stress causing syncope of non-initial vowels from the 5th c. BC), the Raetic inscriptions show no syncope, so Raetic either had no word-initial stress or only a weak one. Stress position is otherwise unrecoverable from the epigraphic record.
new_statements.exceptions: Salomon flags the inference as contested ('but cf. Rix 1985, 117f., and Agostiniani 1992, 52'). Prehistoric apocope of final vowels (shared with Etruscan) is noted elsewhere in the paper (pp. 271, 291) but is not attributed to stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, inferred from spelling of inscriptional forms (names and formulae); no phrase-level or citation-form information is available for a corpus language.
new_statements.identity_note: Raetic (raet1238, ISO xrr) is a corpus language attested only in c. 300 short North-Italic-alphabet inscriptions from Trentino, South/North Tyrol and adjacent areas, 6th–1st c. BC; a Tyrsenian language related to Etruscan and Lemnian (per Rix 1998, Schumacher 1998/2004, Salomon 2020). No dialect subdivision is detectable in the corpus. Not to be confused with Rhaeto-Romance (Romansh, Ladin), which is unrelated. Stress is not recoverable from the script; every statement is inferential (from the absence of Etruscan-type syncope).
